info.name: Billing — Complete
info.description:
The whole billing module: **products → plans → subscriptions → usage → invoices → payments**.

Supersedes `BillingProducts` and `BillingPlans`, which cover only steps 1–2.

## Access model

| | dooit | client |
|---|---|---|
| catalogue & plans | author, publish, version | read what is visible to them |
| subscriptions | provision for anyone | **subscribe / change / cancel** own |
| usage | record, bulk-ingest, reverse | read own |
| invoices | close, issue, void | read own |
| payments | record, retry, refund | read own |

A client who guesses another account's id gets **404**, never 403 — existence is not disclosed.

## Billing model (Model B)

The base fee buys a quota of **applicants**. Usage of products the plan entitles is
covered by that quota and bills nothing — those lines appear on the invoice at
**A$0.00, marked "included"**. Only applicants beyond the allowance bill, at the
overage price. The **6 · End-to-end** folder proves this: 818 metered events across
200 applicants produce an invoice of exactly **A$1,900.00**.

Two rules sit alongside it:

- **Usage outside the plan is charged at list price**, per event, and never
  consumes the applicant allowance. It appears as its own invoice line flagged
  `isExcluded`. A zero-amount line is therefore always `isIncluded` — already paid
  for by the base fee. A line is never both.
- **A negotiated discount** (percentage or fixed) lives on the *subscription*, not
  in the frozen price snapshot, so dooit can renegotiate it. Each invoice copies
  the discount it applied, so history stays reproducible. See **3b**.

## Setup
1. Set `URL` (default `http://localhost:6830`), and the four credential variables.
2. Run **0 · Auth** — captures `{{token}}` and `{{clientToken}}`.
3. Run **6 · End-to-end** top to bottom for a full pass over the module.

Every request asserts its status, so the collection runs as a smoke suite:

```
newman run Billing.postman_collection.json --env-var URL=http://localhost:6830
```

Reference: docs/billingmodule/mongoose-schema.md

Only drafts can be deleted; published plans must be archived.

item.name: 3 · Subscriptions
item.description: The one collection a CLIENT writes to. Note the client token on the writes.

request.description: Freezes the plan pricing into priceSnapshot — billing reads that, never the plan.
Supersedes rather than mutates — a NEW subscription with its own snapshot.

Percentage or fixed, against the whole invoice SUBTOTAL. Takes effect at the
next close — invoices already produced copied the discount they applied, so
this never rewrites a total the customer has been shown.

That is also why the discount lives on the subscription and NOT in
priceSnapshot: the snapshot is frozen, and a negotiated rate has to stay
renegotiable. Send { "type": "none" } to clear it.

item.name: 3b · Discount rules
item.description: A concession on price is dooit-only, like pause — never self-service.

item.name: Assign a plan WITH a discount

request.description: dooit provisioning on a client's behalf, discount attached at assignment.
Capped at the subtotal at billing time — an invoice never goes negative.
It would invert the invoice, so it is refused rather than clamped.
Rejected, not ignored — silently dropping it would let a client believe they had bought at a discount.

item.name: 4 · Usage
item.description: Append-only metering. Writes are dooit/system; a client never self-reports.

request.description: The idempotency key is composed as source:externalId:productCode:ordinal.
Note events 1 and 2 share an externalId but differ by product — both must record.

byProduct, byDay, and DISTINCT applicants — the allowance denominator.

`byProduct` is ENTITLED usage; `excludedByProduct` is usage of products the
plan does not cover, which bills at list price per event and never consumes
the applicant allowance. The split is on `exclusionReason`, not on status, so
a product does not jump buckets the moment its period closes.
Backs the manual-entry picker so applicantKey is chosen, never typed.
Appends a NEGATIVE record. The original is never edited.

query.description: draft | open | paid | overdue | void | all

exec: console.log('sent to', m.sentTo, '| pdf attached:', m.pdfAttached);

request.description:
Renders the document, attaches it as a PDF and mails it. `to` overrides the
delivery address for a one-off (an accounts-payable mailbox) without changing
who the invoice is addressed to — leave it empty to use the account address.

Needs SMTP_EMAIL configured; 503 if this deployment cannot send mail.
sentAt is NOT stamped when delivery fails, so the record never claims a
customer was invoiced when nothing left the building.

exec: // Guards a real regression: page.pdf() returns a Uint8Array, and Express
// JSON-serialises anything that is not a Buffer — a clean 200 carrying
// {"0":37,"1":80,...} under a .pdf filename. Only the bytes catch it.

request.description:
Binary — the same renderer the emailed copy uses, so the attachment and the
download can never disagree about a total.

Returns 503 (not 500) when the host has no headless browser installed:
that is a deployment fault affecting every invoice, not a bad document.
Moves issued invoices past their due date to overdue.
DESTRUCTIVE for the run — released usage can be re-invoiced. Skip in a normal pass.
Flips status WITHOUT a payment record — nothing to refund or reconcile. Prefer 7 · Payments.

item.name: 6 · End-to-end (run in order)
item.description:
The whole money path, and the proof of Model B.

818 metered events across 200 distinct applicants, against a plan with a
5,000-applicant allowance, must invoice **A$1,900.00** — the base fee alone.
Entitled usage appears at A$0.00 marked "included".

request.description: 40 events, 20 distinct applicants — one applicant using two products counts ONCE.

exec: pm.test('entitled usage is included at zero', () => {
// Anything outside the plan is charged, so it is NOT marked included.
pm.test('total is the base fee', () => pm.expect(d.total).to.eql(1900));

request.description: Omitting `amount` settles the whole outstanding balance.
The invoice stays owing; the attempt is kept for the dunning history.
A NEW record chained via retryOf — the failed one is never edited.
Its own record with a POSITIVE amount — `type` carries the direction.
By design: the catalogue names the rows on their invoices.
